{
  "problem_id": "tmm_problem_cf712123ca1f601b",
  "original_request": "Design a planar two-layer antireflection coating on a semi-infinite glass substrate (constant refractive index 1.52, lossless), with air incidence (index 1.0). Use only lossless constant-index SiO2 (n=1.46) and TiO2 (n=2.40), one layer of each in either order. Each layer thickness must be between 40 and 160 nm. At normal incidence with s polarization, minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance sampled from 450 to 700 nm at 5 nm spacing. A mean reflectance below 0.03 is the stated target. Use deterministic TMM only, with no RCWA, FDFD, learned surrogate or hardware. Allow at most two executed research rounds with one route and at most 64 solver evaluations per round, seed 17. After observing the actual result, choose a justified adjustment or stop. Do not claim the target was met without the spectrum and independent numeric check.",
  "normalized_request_english": "Design a planar two-layer antireflection coating on a semi-infinite glass substrate (refractive index 1.52, lossless) with air incidence (refractive index 1.0). The stack must consist of exactly one layer of SiO2 (n=1.46) and one layer of TiO2 (n=2.40), arranged in either order. Each layer thickness is constrained between 40 nm and 160 nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence, sampled from 450 nm to 700 nm in 5 nm steps. A mean reflectance below 0.03 is a stated soft target preference. The method must use deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) only, excluding RCWA, FDFD, learned surrogates, or hardware acceleration. The optimization allows at most two research rounds with one route and up to 64 solver evaluations per round using seed 17. The process requires observing results before deciding on adjustments or stopping, and claims of meeting the target require spectral evidence and independent numeric verification.",
  "primary_intent": "design",
  "secondary_intents": [
    "optimize"
  ],
  "compatibility": "compatible",
  "compatibility_reason": "The request specifies a planar, laterally uniform, linear, isotropic layered medium under frequency-domain plane-wave illumination, which fits the solver boundary. It uses standard materials and TMM without unsupported features like gratings, anisotropy, or time-domain calculations.",
  "wavelengths_nm": [
    [
      450.0,
      700.0
    ]
  ],
  "angles_deg": [
    0.0
  ],
  "polarizations": [
    "s"
  ],
  "target_observables": [
    "reflectance"
  ],
  "preferred_behaviors": [
    "minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm",
    "achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference"
  ],
  "suppressed_behaviors": [
    "high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band"
  ],
  "known_stack_materials": [
    "incident medium: air (n=1.0)",
    "layer candidate 1: SiO2 (n=1.46, lossless)",
    "layer candidate 2: TiO2 (n=2.40, lossless)",
    "substrate: glass (n=1.52, lossless, semi-infinite)"
  ],
  "design_variables": [
    "layer order (SiO2/TiO2 or TiO2/SiO2)",
    "thickness of SiO2 layer (40 nm to 160 nm)",
    "thickness of TiO2 layer (40 nm to 160 nm)"
  ],
  "manufacturing_constraints": [
    "layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm",
    "exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2"
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "refractive indices are constant over the specified wavelength range",
    "interfaces are perfectly planar and abrupt"
  ],
  "ambiguities": [],
  "method_research_questions": [
    "which layer ordering yields the lower global minimum reflectance",
    "whether the 0.03 mean reflectance target is achievable within the thickness constraints",
    "how to justify adjustments after the first research round based on observed spectra"
  ],
  "needs_method_research": false
}
